entries.wants: paragraph for `hmz epic`: An epic is one run of a flow, held by the daemon on a host of its workspace. These commands start one, follow it, say lines to its agents, answer its questions and stop it. Each names the epic by `--workspace` and `--slot`; without them, the epic of the current directory's own host. -- keep every `{name}` in braces and everything in backticks exactly

entries.wants: paragraph for `hmz epic start`: Starts a flow as a new epic held by the daemon, and returns as soon as it has started; the epic runs on without this command. Roles, environments, params and the budget are written as `hmz exec` takes them. Questions the epic asks wait for `hmz epic answer`, unless `--away` is given. `--slot exec:` gives it a host of its own, beside any other epic of the workspace. `--follow` stays and writes the epic as `hmz epic attach` does, and exits with status 1 where the epic failed. -- keep every `{name}` in braces and everything in backticks exactly; up to 90 words
entries.where: paragraph of --help
entries.text: Starts a flow as a new epic held by the daemon, and returns as soon as it has started; the epic runs on without this command. Roles, environments, params and the budget are written as `hmz exec` takes them. Questions the epic asks wait for `hmz epic answer`, unless `--away` is given. `--slot exec:` gives it a host of its own, beside any other epic of the workspace. `--follow` stays and writes the epic as `hmz epic attach` does, and exits with status 1 where the epic failed.
